confirmedNewDefects.scope: 100% -- 10/10 offered Elizabeth-prefixed directions (Stratford x5, Tottenham Court Road x5, the only 2 catalog stations offering Elizabeth-line directions) never match, at every sample taken
confirmedNewDefects.rootCause: TfL's raw lineName for the Elizabeth line is the literal string "Elizabeth line" (not "Elizabeth"). lib/providers/uk-tfl.js builds fullDestination as `${lineName} ${destination}`, so every parsed trip reads e.g. "Elizabeth line Heathrow Terminal 4" while the catalog's offered direction is "Elizabeth Heathrow Terminal 4" -- never equal. normalizeDestination has no rule that strips a trailing " line" token from the line-name portion of the string (lineNameToId does this but only for URL construction, never for the display/matching path).
confirmedNewDefects.suggestedFixDirection: Strip a trailing /\s+line$/i from lineName before building fullDestination (or add "Elizabeth line" -> "Elizabeth" as a normalizeDestination/line alias) -- flagged, not fixed, per Mark's lane

confirmedNewDefects.scope: 100% -- 66/66 offered "Piccadilly Heathrow Terminal 4"/"Piccadilly Heathrow Terminal 5" instances across 33 stations never match, at every sample taken
confirmedNewDefects.rootCause: For Piccadilly-line Heathrow-branch trains, TfL's `towards` field carries a branch-loop label ("Heathrow via T4 Loop", "Heathrow via T5 Loop", "Heathrow T123 + 5"), not the terminal name. parseTflArrival prefers a non-blank, non-compass `towards` over `destinationName`, so the branch-loop text is used as rawDestination; normalizeDestination's `.replace(/\s+via\s+.*$/i, "")` strips the " via T4/T5 Loop" part, collapsing both terminals to bare "Heathrow" -- which matches neither offered direction. destinationName itself ("Heathrow Terminal 4 Underground Station"/"...5...") would normalize correctly if used instead.
confirmedNewDefects.suggestedFixDirection: Prefer destinationName over a "via ... Loop" towards value for this branch (or special-case strip " via T4/T5 Loop" to retain the terminal number instead of discarding it) -- flagged, not fixed

confirmedNewDefects.scope: 86% -- 265/308 offered DLR-prefixed directions show 0 matching trips at capture time, across 44 of the DLR-served catalog stations
confirmedNewDefects.rootCause: TfL's DLR /Arrivals feed sometimes reuses the same `id` field across rows with genuinely different destinationName/platform/timeToStation (confirmed live at Abbey Road: id 322784161 shared by 3 rows going to Woolwich Arsenal, Beckton, and Stratford International at three different times; confirmed again at Beckton Park: id -1340095081 shared by rows to both Tower Gateway and Beckton). fetchStopBoard's allTripsMap dedupes by `trip.id` (`arrival.id || arrival.vehicleId || ...`), so when TfL's id collides across distinct destinations, only one of the colliding trips survives -- the others (often to a completely different, otherwise-real, offered direction) are silently dropped from the board.

evidence.note: 6 rows, 2 genuinely distinct destinations (Tower Gateway, Beckton), only 1 survives dedup

confirmedNewDefects.caveat: This is the largest-by-volume defect found. NOT confirmed row-by-row for all 44 stations -- confirmed live at 2 (Abbey Road, Beckton Park); the other 42 are inferred from the same raw-row-count-vs-parsed-trip-count gap signature (rawRowCount - parsedTripCount > 2, all on the Arrivals/DLR path where every row should otherwise parse). High confidence given the mechanism is now understood and DLR is a single shared feed quirk, but not each station individually live-verified.
confirmedNewDefects.suggestedFixDirection: Stop deduping DLR trips by TfL's raw prediction id; use a composite key that includes destinationNaptanId (e.g. naptanId+destinationNaptanId+timeToStation) so genuinely distinct destinations never collide -- flagged, not fixed
